summary: THE STORED PREMISE FAILS, AND IT FAILS BY TRANSPOSITION. The batch-18 record puts 'Dog of the Military?' and 'The Military Festival' on ep 37 and says ep 13 is stored canon on 'the same basis'. Those two extras are EP 13's — ep 37 adapts two DIFFERENT Arakawa extras. fma.fandom's Episode 37 notes: 'The first part of the episode is adapted from the content of the Bonus Chapter: Roy Mustang's Observation Diary, while the Bachelor Lieutenant portion of the episode is adapted from content in Bonus Chapter: The Second Lieutenant Goes to Battle!, and the Warehouse 13 part is adapted from a mini-story in the first FMA Light Novel: The Land of Sand'; the LICENSOR agrees on segment 1 — Bandai Channel's own synopsis for 第37話 reads 軍内務課からマスタング大佐の監査命令をうけるハボック少尉。彼はブレダ、ファルマン、フュリーとともに「ロイ・マスタング観察日記」を極秘につけはじめる, naming the bonus chapter by its exact title; ja-WP's segment title for the middle third is 「戦う少尉さん」, which is the exact Japanese title of the vol-7 gaiden (en-WP's volume list: 'The Second Lieutenant Goes to Battle!' 戦う 少尉さん). fma.fandom's Episode 13 notes, independently corroborated by SlashFilm's 2026 piece on the episode, say ep 13 adapts 'The Military Festival' (vol 3 gaiden) and 'Dog of the Military?' (vol 4 gaiden) — plus, per SlashFilm, the vol-4 four-panel omake 'The Ambitious Alchemist' (Mustang's miniskirt declaration; the fandom's Volume 4 page lists that omake in the volume's back matter). So the two rows adapt four different Arakawa extras between them and the stored ep-37 label is simply ep 13's label. NEITHER ROW CAN BE ANCHORED: every piece of source material on both rows is an UNNUMBERED gaiden or omake printed in the tankōbon back matter (MangaDex's scanlation feed has to invent 12.5 / 16.5 / 29.5 for them; en-WP's volume list prints them as 'Gaiden.' with no number and omits the prose Observation Diary entirely) — A44 position-less, and nothing in the position line moves. BOTH ROWS ARE MIXED, NOT CANON. Ep 37 (T28 segment accounting, both halves story-carrying): segments 1+2 = Arakawa's own bonus chapters, roughly 13 of ~23 minutes (fandom: segment 1 is 'the shortest and serves as a cold open', segment 2 'takes up half of the remaining runtime'); segment 3 = the novel's bonus short 'The Phantom of Warehouse 13' — which a licence does not make canon (T26, 2026-09-05) — plus a large 2003-ORIGINAL serial thread woven through it (Sheska hired by Frank Archer to reconstruct the Lab 5 / Marcoh / Tucker files, Archer having the report destroyed, Archer approved by Bradley to move on Reole with Kimblee and Tucker, Mustang requesting to join) which CANNOT be novel material: Archer is exclusive to the 2003 anime (fandom: 'an antagonist exclusive to the Fullmetal Alchemist 2003 anime series', first cameo ep 25) and The Land of Sand was published in February 2003. en-WP calls segment 3 'the other half of the episode'. Source ~55%, non-source ~45%, both story-carrying = MIXED. Ep 13: the two gaiden are 11 pages each on MangaDex (against 32-52 pages for a numbered chapter) and the omake is four panels — call it 10-12 minutes of a 23-minute episode; the rest is anime-original and it is the arc-launching plot, not framing. The gaiden's duel is brokered by a barracks argument over who is stronger and ends with Ed 'soundly defeated'; the ANIME rebuilds the premise (Ed wagers the duel to extract Dr. Marcoh's whereabouts — a thread that exists only because eps 11-12 adapted the novel's Xenotime story) and rebuilds the ending (a draw, because Mustang freezes on an Ishbal flashback), and it adds Grand's entourage and Bradley's move to Eastern Command with the secretary Juliet Douglas whom Ed eyes suspiciously (Sloth's planting), Grand branding Marcoh a deserter, Ed's failed archive search, Mustang's tip, and the closing Hughes/Mustang bar scene that puts Scar on the road to East City. The licensor's own one-paragraph description of ep 13 is that original thread, not the duel: 国家錬金術師としての調査報告のために、軍・東方司令部を訪れたエドとアル。エドはゼノタイムで聞いたドクター・マルコーの噂を、マスタング大佐に尋ねてみるが軽くかわされてしまう。そこでエドは一計を案じ… So ep 13 = three Arakawa extras + a substantial, story-carrying anime-original half = MIXED. The ep-13 flip is the one judgment in this verdict (the facts are settled; the SHARE is what decides canon vs mixed) — flagged for Sean with the alternative reading stated. Both rows keep / gain a side_story annotation, which is WEIGHT-BEARING under lib/side-source.ts, so ep 37's mixed standing survives the T26 writer default despite its side_source record.

anchor_hostile.why: A44 position-less — the row is MIXED (not filler, so this is not an A1 refusal) and its source share is significant, but EVERY page it adapts sits outside the numbered chapter space. 'The Military Festival' (軍部の祭り) is the unnumbered gaiden printed at the back of tankōbon vol 3 (2002-09-21) and 'Dog of the Military?' (軍の犬?) the unnumbered gaiden at the back of vol 4 (2003-01-22); 'The Ambitious Alchemist' is a four-panel omake in vol 4's back matter. en-WP's volume list prints both gaiden as '* [[Gaiden]].' with no chapter number where every mainline entry is '* 009.' / '* 013.'; MangaDex's scanlation feed can only carry them as invented decimals (vol 3 ch 12.5 'Gaiden - Military Festival', 11 pages; vol 4 ch 16.5 'Gaiden - Dog Of The Military?', 11 pages), which is a scanlator's sort key, not the printed numbering (N35: deliver PRINTED numbers, and there is no printed number here). Nothing mainline is stranded by declining: ep 13 does not adapt any numbered chapter — the mainline material around it is ep 8's pulled-forward ch 24 behind it and ch 6-7 (Scar) in eps 14-15 ahead of it, and no numbered page of the manga is left unaccounted by refusing this row a number. The extras are recorded as FACTS in the side_story annotation (title, Japanese title, which volume's back matter, page count, which numbered chapters they sit between) exactly as the catalog handles 番外編 material.

A44 position-less — the row is MIXED and its source share is significant (segments 1 and 2, ~13 of ~23 minutes), but neither piece carries a chapter number. 'The Second Lieutenant Goes to Battle!' (戦う 少尉さん) is the unnumbered gaiden at the back of tankōbon vol 7 (2004-03-22; MangaDex has to file it as 29.5, 9 pages); 'Roy Mustang's Observation Diary' (ロイ・マスタング観察日記) is a PROSE bonus piece in vol 6's back matter (2003-10-22) — fma.fandom: 'Differently from other bonus chapters, this one is not made out of images, but written exactly like a Journal… Images are occasional' — which is why en-WP's volume list, which prints the vol-3/4/7 gaiden, has no entry for it at all and MangaDex's comic feed has none either. The third segment is a licensed NOVEL's bonus short (The Land of Sand), a different work in a different space entirely (T26). No mainline chapter is stranded: the run's manga contact around here is ch 30's Martel beat grafted into eps 40-41, and ep 37 touches no numbered page.

annotations.chapters: FMA bonus chapters: 'Roy Mustang's Observation Diary' (ロイ・マスタング観察日記, unnumbered prose gaiden in tankōbon vol 6's back matter, 2003-10-22, between ch 25 and ch 26) = segment 1 'The Flame Alchemist' 焔の錬金術師; 'The Second Lieutenant Goes to Battle!' (戦う 少尉さん, unnumbered gaiden in tankōbon vol 7's back matter, 9 pp, 2004-03-22, between ch 29 and ch 30) = segment 2 'The Bachelor Lieutenant' 戦う少尉さん
annotations.note: REPLACES the stored label, which named ep 13's two extras by mistake (see repairs). SEGMENT 1 = the Observation Diary: Havoc is ordered by the military's internal-affairs section to conduct that year's efficiency evaluation of his own commanding officer and enlists Breda, Falman and Fuery to keep a secret log of Mustang's working day; the log's jokes (the paperwork left to the last minute, the office cleaned for inspection, the failed attempts to befriend Hawkeye's dog) and its punchline (Havoc docked half a month's pay for neglecting his own job while Mustang is commended) are the segment. The licensor names the piece outright: Bandai Channel 第37話 — 軍内務課からマスタング大佐の監査命令をうけるハボック少尉。彼はブレダ、ファルマン、フュリーとともに「ロイ・マスタング観察日記」を極秘につけはじめる。 SEGMENT 2 = the vol-7 gaiden, beat for beat: Havoc dumped for putting work first, Mustang ordering Armstrong to find him a woman, the Armstrong Manor, Philip Gargantos Armstrong's speech on the family's 180 years, Mrs. Armstrong's height, Catherine's beauty and the shared Armstrong eyelashes, the piano she likes to lift with her bare hands, Havoc asking her out and being turned down because she only wants a man as strong as her brother. ja-WP's segment title is the gaiden's own title 「戦う少尉さん」; the gaiden's own trivia says 'The events of this chapter would be adapted into parts of Episode 37'. weight: SIGNIFICANT — because the two extras ARE the plot of the episode's first two segments and together take roughly 13 of ~23 minutes (fandom: segment 1 is 'the shortest and serves as a cold open', segment 2 'takes up half of the remaining runtime'); neither is adapted anywhere else in the 51-episode run. THE OBSERVATION DIARY'S VOLUME PLACEMENT IS SINGLE-SOURCE (fma.fandom's chapter page and its Volume 6 'Chapters Included' list); en-WP's volume list and MangaDex both omit it because it is prose, not a drawn chapter — the FACT that ep 37 segment 1 adapts it has two sources (fandom + the licensor's title-naming synopsis), the vol-6 placement has one, and that is stated rather than smoothed over.

annotations.chapters: The Land of Sand: 'The Phantom of Warehouse 13' — the bonus short printed after the epilogue of the first FMA light novel 『鋼の錬金術師 砂礫の大地』 (Makoto Inoue, illustrated by Arakawa; Square Enix, February 2003) = segment 3 'The Mystery of Warehouse 13' 第十三倉庫の怪
annotations.note: The stored record was right about the work and the segment; this refines the label (the piece is the NOVEL's bonus short, listed in its contents after 'Prologue / 1 Golden Hair / 2 Silver Eyes / 3 Crimson Water / Epilogue' as 'Bonus: The Phantom of Warehouse 13') and drops the sentence that mis-stated ep 13's basis. NO STANDING, NO ADOPTION (T26, the sitting of 2026-09-05): Inoue wrote it and Arakawa only illustrated the volume; there is no act by the source's author taking this story into the manga line, and an illustrator's name on a cover is exactly the blanket credit T26 rejects. weight: NONE toward canon — this segment counts as NON-SOURCE in the standing, and together with the anime-original Archer/Sheska thread inside the same segment (see the divergence record) it is the half of the episode that makes the row MIXED rather than canon. INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION THAT THE NOVEL IS THE SEGMENT'S SOURCE: en-WP's light-novel article, citing Square Enix's own hagaren novel page, states 'The first novel of the series, Fullmetal Alchemist: The Land of Sand, was used as the source material for episodes 11, 12 and part of 37 of the first Fullmetal Alchemist anime adaptation'; fma.fandom's Episode 37 notes say the Warehouse 13 part 'is adapted from a mini-story in the first FMA Light Novel'. Same work as the stored eps 11/12 side_source record — the catalog is consistent across the three rows.

THE ANIME-ORIGINAL SERIAL THREAD INSIDE SEGMENT 3 — the record that makes this row's non-source half more than a novel short. Interleaved with the haunted-warehouse comedy, ep 37 runs the 2003 series' own plot: Lt. Colonel Frank Archer hires Sheska on a provisional basis to reconstruct the destroyed files on Basque Grand, Marcoh and Tucker and the Laboratory 5 / Central Prison incidents; Sheska accepts so she can hunt for a lead on Hughes' death; Archer reads her completed report and orders it destroyed over her objections; Archer tells Bradley he believes there is a conspiracy inside the military, receives approval to put down the Reole uprising with Kimblee and Tucker under his command, and learns Scar has gone to ground; Mustang then asks the Führer to be sent with Archer and Armstrong to Reole. This CANNOT come from the novel: Frank Archer is 'an antagonist exclusive to the Fullmetal Alchemist 2003 anime series' (fma.fandom), first seen in a cameo in ep 25 and introduced properly in ep 29, and The Land of Sand was published in February 2003, fifteen months before this episode aired. It is also the setup for eps 38-41 (Reole, Kimblee, Tucker), i.e. story-carrying rather than framing. Also recorded: Mustang burning a secret message from Armstrong, and the Winry-at-the-window beat at the Hughes house — both 2003-original continuity. Combined with the novel short, the non-source share of this episode is ~45% and self-contained, which is the T28 basis for MIXED.

annotations.chapters: FMA bonus chapters: 'The Military Festival' (軍部の祭り, unnumbered gaiden in tankōbon vol 3's back matter, 11 pp, 2002-09-21, between ch 12 and ch 13) — the Mustang vs. Edward exhibition match; 'Dog of the Military?' (軍の犬?, unnumbered gaiden in tankōbon vol 4's back matter, 11 pp, 2003-01-22, between ch 16 and ch 17) — Fuery's stray puppy, Al's hidden cat, Hawkeye adopting Black Hayate; 'The Ambitious Alchemist' (four-panel omake, tankōbon vol 4 back matter) — Mustang's miniskirt declaration
annotations.note: A NEW record: the stored row carried no annotation at all, so nothing said WHAT ep 13 adapts — and the ep-37 record's claim that ep 13 rests on 'the same basis' as ep 37 is wrong twice over (different extras, and ep 37 also carries a novel segment ep 13 has none of). fma.fandom's Episode 13 notes: 'This episode is adapted from the material of the manga bonus chapters Dog of the Military? and The Military Festival'; both gaiden pages say the same from the other direction ('The events of this Bonus Chapter would be adapted into parts of Episode 13: Fullmetal vs. Flame'), and SlashFilm's 2026 piece on the episode independently reports the same pair plus the omake ('to expand the runtime, the episode incorporates two other bonus chapters: Dog of the Military… and a non-canonical four-panel omake titled The Ambitious Alchemist'), with the fandom's Volume 4 page listing 'The Ambitious Alchemist: Part 2' among that volume's omake. WHAT IS IN THE EPISODE, PIECE BY PIECE. From 'The Military Festival': the argument over who would win, Ed being in East City for his annual State Alchemist assessment, Hughes brokering the parade grounds, Bradley approving the match, the crowd, Ed's coat decoy, the destroyed ignition glove and Mustang's second glove up the other sleeve, the Führer ordering everyone to clean up the wrecked grounds, Hughes drinking coffee through it ('a soldier should know when to retreat'). From 'Dog of the Military?': Fuery's rain-soaked puppy, Breda's terror of dogs, Havoc's stir-fry joke, the Elrics refusing because they travel, Al hiding a cat in his armour and running off crying, Mustang's 'faithful servants' line, Hawkeye taking the dog and firing a ring of shots around it for wetting the floor (the anime even reproduces the chapter's own art error — seven holes for six shots). From the omake: Mustang's declaration that as Führer he would put every female officer in a miniskirt. weight: SIGNIFICANT for the two gaiden — they are 11 pages each (MangaDex's page counts, against 32-52 pages for a numbered chapter) and they carry the episode's title fight and its running B-plot, roughly 10-12 minutes of a ~23-minute episode; weight: SLIVER for the four-panel omake — a single gag scene, no story weight, noted so it stays visible. None of the three is adapted in any other episode of the run. DIRECTION IS CLEAN: vol 3 shipped 2002-09-21 and vol 4 2003-01-22, both a year or more before this episode aired on 2003-12-27 (the GTO/souleater trap does not apply).

THE 2003-ORIGINAL HALF OF EP 13 — the record the row lacked, and the basis for the mixed typing. (a) THE PREMISE IS REPLACED. In the gaiden the exhibition match happens because a barracks argument about who is stronger gets out of hand; in the anime Ed proposes it as a WAGER — if he wins, Mustang tells him about the travelling alchemist doctor — a thread that exists only because eps 11-12 adapted the novel's Xenotime story (Belsio's tip). The licensor's own synopsis of the episode is that thread, not the duel: 国家錬金術師としての調査報告のために、軍・東方司令部を訪れたエドとアル。エドはゼノタイムで聞いたドクター・マルコーの噂を、マスタング大佐に尋ねてみるが軽くかわされてしまう。そこでエドは一計を案じ… (b) THE OUTCOME IS REPLACED. The gaiden ends 'with a huge, final blast, Edward is soundly defeated'; the anime ends in a DRAW because Mustang freezes on an Ishbal flashback, which is then the hook for Mustang's tip and for eps 14-15. (c) ADDED ORIGINAL PLOT, none of it in any extra: the Reole debrief; Brigadier General Grand arriving with the Führer's entourage to make Eastern Command a temporary HQ; the Führer's secretary Juliet Douglas (Sloth) whom Ed eyes with suspicion — the 2003 series planting its own endgame; Grand branding Marcoh a deserter and traitor; Hughes' promotion to Lt. Colonel and head of Investigations; Ed's failed search of the archives; and the closing Hughes/Mustang bar scene (Reole is still in strife under Hakuro, Mustang decides to keep it from Ed, Scar is confirmed to be moving on East City). Roughly half the runtime, and it is the material eps 14-15 run on. Under T28's faithfulness clause (a) and (b) alone would be divergence on a canon row; it is (c) — a story-carrying original share — that makes the row mixed.

type_corrections.note: canon (T6 pin, batch 18) -> MIXED. T28 segment accounting on an episode the wiki and en-WP both describe structurally, so the shares are sourced rather than guessed. SEGMENT 1 'The Flame Alchemist' — SOURCE (Arakawa's vol-6 prose bonus 'Roy Mustang's Observation Diary'); fandom: 'the shortest and serves as a cold open', ~3 minutes; weight: SIGNIFICANT (it is the whole segment's plot, adapted nowhere else). SEGMENT 2 'The Bachelor Lieutenant' — SOURCE (Arakawa's vol-7 gaiden 'The Second Lieutenant Goes to Battle!', 9 pp); fandom: 'takes up half of the remaining runtime', ~10 minutes; weight: SIGNIFICANT (beat for beat the gaiden, ending on Catherine's rejection). SEGMENT 3 'The Mystery of Warehouse 13' — NON-SOURCE, and doubly so: (i) the licensed novel's bonus short, which under T26 (the sitting of 2026-09-05) confers no standing — a licence is not adoption, Inoue wrote it and Arakawa only illustrated the volume, and there is no adopted{basis} act; (ii) woven through it, a 2003-anime-original serial thread (Sheska hired by Archer, the report destroyed, Archer approved to march on Reole with Kimblee and Tucker, Mustang asking to go) that CANNOT be novel material because Archer is exclusive to the 2003 anime and the novel predates him by fifteen months. fandom: the segment 'takes up the second half of the episode'; en-WP: 'In the other half of the episode…'. So ~55% source, ~45% non-source, both halves self-contained and story-carrying (segment 3 sets up eps 38-41) = the T28 definition of MIXED: source and non-source in one episode. NOT FILLER — the manga extras are a weight-bearing side_story tie, so lib/side-source.ts's T26 default does not fire (WEIGHT_BEARING_KINDS includes side_story); NOT CANON — the stored canon rested on the very extras that turn out to be ep 13's, and on treating the novel half as source, which the 2026-09-05 sitting removed. WHAT THE TYPE SOURCES SAY, AND WHY THEY ARE NOT THE WITNESS: AFL prints 'Filler' for this row (it reads the whole episode as a gag interlude and cannot see the two tankōbon extras); AFL and AFG are one lineage and neither is a type witness (batch-21 wave-1 ruling). The witness here is the segment map plus the shares, both sourced twice.

canon (stored, AFL 'Manga Canon') -> MIXED. THIS IS THE ONE JUDGMENT IN THE VERDICT and it is a SHARE judgment, not a fact dispute: what ep 13 adapts is settled twice over (fma.fandom's episode notes + both gaiden pages' reverse index + SlashFilm's independent account). SOURCE SHARE: 'The Military Festival' (vol 3 gaiden, 11 pp) = the duel, and 'Dog of the Military?' (vol 4 gaiden, 11 pp) = the Black Hayate / Al's-cat runner, plus the four-panel omake 'The Ambitious Alchemist' (weight: sliver). 22 gaiden pages against 32-52 pages for a numbered chapter, i.e. roughly half a chapter's worth of pages carrying maybe 10-12 minutes of a ~23-minute episode; weight: SIGNIFICANT for the two gaiden (the duel is the episode's title and climax; the dog story is its B-plot from cold open to tag). NON-SOURCE SHARE, and why it is not mere framing: the anime REPLACES the gaiden's premise (the fight is fought as a wager for Dr. Marcoh's whereabouts — a thread that exists only because eps 11-12 adapted the novel) and its outcome (a draw on Mustang's Ishbal flashback, where the gaiden has Ed 'soundly defeated'), and adds a full act of 2003-original serial plot: Grand's entourage and Bradley's move to Eastern Command, the secretary Juliet Douglas (Sloth) whom Ed eyes suspiciously, Grand branding Marcoh a deserter, Hughes' promotion and Ed's failed archive search, Mustang's tip, and the closing bar scene that puts Scar on the road to East City and keeps Reole's collapse from Ed. That material is what eps 14-15 run on — story-carrying by any reading, and roughly half the runtime. The licensor's own synopsis describes the episode AS that thread (国家錬金術師としての調査報告のために…エドはゼノタイムで聞いたドクター・マルコーの噂を…そこでエドは一計を案じ) and en-WP's summary gives it four of its six sentences. Source + anime-original, both substantial and story-carrying, in one episode = MIXED (T25/T27/T28), and it matches how this series is already curated (ep 21 is mixed for exactly this shape: the manga's Lab 5 story with Scar/Greed/Kimblee grafted in). THE ALTERNATIVE READING, STATED HONESTLY: if the episode's 'job' is taken to be the duel alone, the original material reads as connective tissue and the row stays CANON with the divergence record — that is what batch 18 held. I deliver mixed because the original share is not connective (it replaces the source's own premise and ending and launches the next arc), but this is Sean's call, and the annotations are correct either way. AFL's 'Manga Canon' is not a type witness (AFL/AFG are one lineage) and in any case cannot distinguish 'adapts a gaiden' from 'adapts a chapter'.

structure.premise_test: THE ASK'S CLAIM TO TEST FAILED (and it is worth recording as a trap): the stored ep-37 note said the episode's two Arakawa extras were 'Dog of the Military?' and 'The Military Festival' and that ep 13 was stored canon on 'the same basis'. Both halves are wrong — those are ep 13's extras, ep 37's are 'Roy Mustang's Observation Diary' (vol 6) and 'The Second Lieutenant Goes to Battle!' (vol 7), and ep 13 carries no novel material at all. The likely mechanism: batch 18 read one wiki page's reverse-index line ('would be adapted into parts of Episode 13') onto the other episode. R20's spirit applies to WORKS as well as rows — join a bonus chapter to an episode on the episode page's own statement AND the chapter page's reverse index, never on one direction alone.
structure.chapter_space: Both rows are entirely outside the numbered chapter space. The FMA manga's printed numbering is 1-108 mainline chapters across 27 volumes (ja-WP: 話数=全108話; our stored total_chapters=116 is AniList's UNIT count, which folds the gaiden/omake in — say which you mean, per the AniList unit-count trap). The gaiden are printed unnumbered in the tankōbon back matter: 'The Military Festival' after ch 12 (vol 3), 'Dog of the Military?' after ch 16 (vol 4), 'Roy Mustang's Observation Diary' after ch 25 (vol 6), 'The Second Lieutenant Goes to Battle!' after ch 29 (vol 7). MangaDex's 12.5 / 16.5 / 29.5 are scanlator sort keys, NOT printed numbers (N35), and its feed has no entry at all for the vol-6 prose piece; en-WP's volume list prints them as 'Gaiden.' with no number and likewise omits the prose piece. Deliver these as side_story FACTS, never as numbers (A44).
structure.row_identity: Both rows join cleanly on title + air date across every source (R20). Ours: 13 'Fullmetal VS Flame' 2003-12-27, 37 'The Flame Alchemist, The Bachelor Lieutenant & The Mystery of Warehouse 13' 2004-06-26.
